post.caption: In 1949, three brothers were digging clay at a tile factory in Panagyurishte, Bulgaria, when they struck a hoard of nine gold vessels. Together the vessels weigh 6.164 kilograms. Thracian goldsmiths made them around 300 BC, so they are about 2,300 years old. Many are rhyta, drinking horns shaped like animals, and the set includes a big amphora and a shallow dish. That dish is inscribed with its own weight, 100 Persian darics. It was found on December 8, 1949.
